issues.failure_explanation: Since L(t) = ηG(t) + √ρ W(G(t)) − ct with G independent of W, V[L(t)] = ηηᵀ V[G(t)] + ρ E[G(t)] = t δ Γ(2−α)/λ^(2−α) (ηηᵀ + ρ λ/(1−α)), using Γ(2−α) = (1−α)Γ(1−α) and the moments of G printed in the appendix. The displayed formula instead has ρλ^(1−α) in place of ρλ/(1−α); the two expressions agree only at α = 0. The appendix Table 'tab: NTS' prints the correct formula, and the paper's own variance table confirms it numerically: for NIG1 (α = 1/2, λ = 57.1108, ρ = [[0.037021, 0.026574],[0.026574, 0.054613]], η = (−0.295846, −0.292984)) the correct formula gives √V[L⁽¹⁾(1)] ≈ 0.1944 (table: 0.1943), whereas the printed formula gives ≈ 0.0567.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ρλ^(1−α) by ρλ/(1−α) in the display (equivalently write V[L(t)] = tδ( Γ(1−α)/λ^(1−α) ρ + Γ(2−α)/λ^(2−α) ηηᵀ )), matching the appendix Table 'tab: NTS'.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed variance formula in the numerical-experiments section is false as stated. No result, the numerical scheme, or the parameter tables rely on it (the variance table was computed with the correct formula), so the impact is confined to the incorrect display itself.
issues.title: Wrong coefficient in the NTS variance formula of the numerical experiments section
issues.why_classification: A single forced correction, identifiable from the paper's own appendix table and confirmed by its numerical variance table and by direct computation; no downstream claim relies on the erroneous formula, so every substantive result survives.

issues.failure_explanation: For the VG0 parameter set (α = 0, λ = 1, η = (−0.1, −0.2), ρ = [[0.09, 0.06],[0.06, 0.16]]) the paper's own formula gives ‖η‖_ρ² = ηᵀρ⁻¹η = 0.0028/0.0108 ≈ 0.2593, hence B_ℓ = √(‖η‖_ρ² + 2λ) − ‖η‖_ρ ≈ 1.5031 − 0.5092 ≈ 0.994 < 2. This violates the standing assumption A_ℓ < 2, B_ℓ > 2 on which the model framework is built, so VG0 is not covered by the framework (the associated exponential Lévy model does not have a finite second moment, since 2 > B_ℓ). The paper nevertheless presents VG0 as one of the four representative experiments and states that common VG and NIG models satisfy the conditions, without any remark; the other three sets do satisfy B_ℓ > 2 (e.g. VG1: B_ℓ ≈ 2.18).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reconcile scope and experiments: weaken the standing assumption to B_ℓ > 0 for the numerical method (noting that B_ℓ ≥ 2 is only needed for the cited finite-variance SDE existence result) and remark explicitly that VG0 lies outside the finite-variance framework but remains a valid test of the scheme; alternatively, exclude VG0 from the framework's coverage.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the numerical experiments instantiate the paper's framework is inaccurate for the VG0 parameter set: the finite-variance hypothesis invoked for the framework does not cover VG0. The numerical scheme itself (quadrature, FFT evaluation, semi-Lagrangian time-stepping) does not rely on B_ℓ > 2, so the empirical convergence results are presumably unaffected, but the inconsistency is undisclosed.
issues.title: VG0 experiment violates the framework's standing assumption B_ℓ > 2
issues.why_classification: A concrete violated hypothesis requiring a scope correction (a limited weakening of a motivated assumption or exclusion of a headline test case) rather than a typo-level fix; the repair is contained and the method's empirical conclusions survive, so it is not serious.
